note: The console's policy, written fresh for this demo. Rules are read top to bottom and the first one that matches a call decides. A call no rule matches is denied. A rule with stop ends the session when it denies. Every condition a rule lists has to hold: the tools it covers, paths (a pattern without a slash matches the file's name, * stays inside a folder and ** crosses folders), command words (a lone * matches any number of words and a word with * in it matches one word), shell operators, hosts, and size limits. {{v1.domain}} and the like are filled in from config/names.json.

rules.label: Anything outside the project
rules.why: Every path is resolved first and anything that lands outside the project folder is refused.

rules.label: Secrets files
rules.why: Secrets are never readable here. Reaching for one ends the session at once so that a person can look into what the agent was after.

rules.label: Pipes, chains and redirects
rules.why: Commands run one at a time with no shell and each one is checked on its own.

rules.label: Network commands
rules.why: Nothing reaches the network from the shell.

rules.label: Destructive or admin commands
rules.why: Commands that delete trees, change permissions or act as another user are never run.

rules.label: Git's settings, remotes and history
rules.why: An agent can commit but it can't rewrite history or point git somewhere else. The rule covers every git config and git remote command including one that only lists them.

rules.label: Pushing to the remote
rules.why: A push is the first thing that leaves the project so a person decides.

rules.label: Installing packages
rules.why: A new dependency is code from outside that a person has to approve.

rules.label: Running the tests
rules.why: Tests are how an agent checks its own work.

rules.label: Running other code
rules.why: Code that isn't a test could do whatever the user could do. A person says yes or no first.

rules.label: Looking around
rules.why: Reading the project is how an agent learns it.

rules.label: Making and moving files
rules.why: Inside the project these are ordinary work.

rules.label: Deleting a file
rules.why: A deleted file is gone for good. A person makes that call.

rules.label: Local git
rules.why: Commits stay on this machine until a push.

rules.label: Large writes
rules.why: A write this big is unusual for these jobs and a person decides.

rules.label: Project files
rules.why: Reading and changing the project's own files is the job.

rules.label: Sending data in an address
rules.why: A long query string is a common way to carry data out and it's refused.

rules.label: Pages on the list
rules.why: The research job reads these three pages through the reader.

rules.label: Any other address
rules.why: A person decides first for anywhere else on the web.
